pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: Python is the most popular programming language in the world. People use it to build websites and bots, analyse data, automate routine work and create AI.
pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.1.html:
• Python developers are paid well — it is one of the most in-demand professions
  • The code reads almost like English
  • You will write your first program within five minutes
pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: This is what Python code looks like — try running it right here:
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: On this site Python runs inside your browser, but for real work you need Python on your computer:
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.1.html:
1. Go to python.org/downloads and download the latest version
  2. Run the installer
  3. ⚠️ Make sure to tick «Add Python to PATH» — this is the single most common beginner mistake!
  4. Click Install Now
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: To verify: open a terminal (Win+R → cmd) and type:
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: An editor (IDE) is a smart text editor: it highlights errors, completes your code and runs programs with one button.
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.1.html:
1. Download the free VS Code from code.visualstudio.com (the one your mentor recommended)
  2. Install it and add the Python extension
  3. Create a file: main.py
  4. Run it: the ▶ button or F5
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Done — your workspace is ready. Now for the code itself.
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: The print() function displays text on screen. Text goes inside quotes — double or single, it makes no difference:
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Notice: print() can output several things separated by commas, and numbers are written without quotes — Python computes them for you.
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.3.html: Comments start with # — Python ignores them, they exist for humans:

• Theory — short cards with examples you can actually run
  • Quiz — check your understanding (70%+ required)
  • Tasks — write real code with automatic checking
  • Exam — a timed test. Pass it and the next level unlocks!
pb-01.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: Everything earns you XP — climb from Novice to Sensei. Study every day so you keep your streak. Let's go!
pb-01.quiz.0.q: Which function prints text to the screen?
pb-01.quiz.0.explain: In Python text is printed with the print() function.
pb-01.quiz.1.q: Which checkbox MUST be ticked when installing Python on Windows?
pb-01.quiz.1.explain: Without «Add Python to PATH» the python command will not work in the terminal.
pb-01.quiz.2.explain: Text in quotes is printed as is. To compute it, write it without quotes: print(5 + 5).
pb-01.quiz.3.q: How does a comment start in Python?
pb-01.quiz.3.explain: Comments in Python start with the # character.
pb-01.quiz.4.explain: VS Code is an editor (IDE) — a program that makes writing and running code comfortable.
pb-01.quiz.5.explain: Numbers without quotes get computed by Python: 3 + 4 = 7.
pb-01.tasks.0.hint: Use print("Привет, Python!") — the text must match exactly, including the exclamation mark.

pb-01.tasks.2.desc: Print the result of 25 * 4 (the number itself, not the text).
pb-01.tasks.2.hint: print(25 * 4) — no quotes! In quotes Python prints text, without them it does the maths.
